newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian prison riots rage on after six killed.
newsitem.headline: Colombian prison riots rage on after six killed.

text.p: Rebellious inmates were in control of several prisons across Colombia on Friday, a day after six inmates were killed and nearly 30 injured in uprisings in Bogota and central Tolima province, authorities said.

A spokesman for the National Prisons Institute said the death toll from Thursday's uprisings was raised to six on Friday morning after one of six prisoners felled by gunshots in the melee in Tolima's Picalena jail died of his injuries.
One other prisoner was shot dead in Picalena and four were killed when guards moved to quell a bloody riot in Bogota's Modelo prison, the spokesman said.
In all, at least 28 inmates were wounded in Bogota and Tolima, he said, adding that Picalena remained firmly in the hands of rioting prisoners on Friday afternoon.

"We're here putting out fires," the spokesman said, noting that other prisons -- including the jam-packed Modelo jail in the Caribbean port city of Barranquilla -- had been under the control of rebel inmates for several days now.

According to Bogota's El Tiempo newspaper, nearly 8,000 prisoners -- or about one-fifth of Colombia's jail population -- have staged riots in penitentiaries across the country this week to protest against severe overcrowding, human rights violations and miserable living conditions.
El Tiempo said the riots appeared to have been planned in advance and may have been organised by leftist guerrillas or drug traffickers.

Authorities have responded to the violence by saying a concerted effort will be made reduce overcrowding. But no one has said exactly how that can be brought about, in the short term, without simply putting prisoners back on the street.
